briefdescription.para: These operations represent an abstract X86 call instruction, which includes a bunch of information.

detaileddescription.para: In particular the operands of these node are: #0 - The incoming token chain #1 - The callee #2 - The number of arg bytes the caller pushes on the stack. #3 - The number of arg bytes the callee pops off the stack. #4 - The value to pass in AL/AX/EAX (optional) #5 - The value to pass in DL/DX/EDX (optional)
The result values of these nodes are: #0 - The outgoing token chain #1 - The first register result value (optional) #2 - The second register result value (optional)

briefdescription.para: Same as call except it adds the NoTrack prefix.
X86 compare and logical compare instructions.
X86 bit-test instructions.
X86 SetCC.

detaileddescription.para: Operand 0 is condition code, and operand 1 is the EFLAGS operand, usually produced by a CMP instruction.

briefdescription.para: X86 Select.
X86 FP SETCC, implemented with CMP{cc}SS/CMP{cc}SD.

detaileddescription.para: Operands are two FP values to compare; result is a mask of 0s or 1s. Generally DTRT for C/C++ with NaNs.

briefdescription.para: X86 FP SETCC, similar to above, but with output as an i1 mask and and a version with SAE.
X86 conditional moves.

detaileddescription.para: Operand 0 and operand 1 are the two values to select from. Operand 2 is the condition code, and operand 3 is the flag operand produced by a CMP or TEST instruction.

briefdescription.para: X86 conditional branches.

detaileddescription.para: Operand 0 is the chain operand, operand 1 is the block to branch if condition is true, operand 2 is the condition code, and operand 3 is the flag operand produced by a CMP or TEST instruction.

briefdescription.para: BRIND node with NoTrack prefix.

detaileddescription.para: Operand 0 is the chain operand and operand 1 is the target address.

briefdescription.para: Return with a glue operand.

detaileddescription.para: Operand 0 is the chain operand, operand 1 is the number of bytes of stack to pop.

briefdescription.para: Return from interrupt. Operand 0 is the number of bytes to pop.

briefdescription.para: This instruction implements FP_TO_SINT with the integer destination in memory and a FP reg source.

detaileddescription.para: This corresponds to the X86::FIST*m instructions and the rounding mode change stuff. It has two inputs (token chain and address) and two outputs (int value and token chain). Memory VT specifies the type to store to.

briefdescription.para: This instruction implements SINT_TO_FP with the integer source in memory and FP reg result.

detaileddescription.para: This corresponds to the X86::FILD*m instructions. It has two inputs (token chain and address) and two outputs (FP value and token chain). The integer source type is specified by the memory VT.

briefdescription.para: This instruction implements a fp->int store from FP stack slots.

detaileddescription.para: This corresponds to the fist instruction. It takes a chain operand, value to store, address, and glue. The memory VT specifies the type to store as.

briefdescription.para: This instruction implements an extending load to FP stack slots.

detaileddescription.para: This corresponds to the X86::FLD32m / X86::FLD64m. It takes a chain operand, and ptr to load from. The memory VT specifies the type to load from.

briefdescription.para: This instruction implements a truncating store from FP stack slots.

detaileddescription.para: This corresponds to the X86::FST32m / X86::FST64m. It takes a chain operand, value to store, address, and glue. The memory VT specifies the type to store as.

briefdescription.para: These instructions grab the address of the next argument from a va_list.

detaileddescription.para: (reads and modifies the va_list in memory)

briefdescription.para: Compare and Add if Condition is Met.

detaileddescription.para: Compare value in operand 2 with value in memory of operand 1. If condition of operand 4 is met, add value operand 3 to m32 and write new value in operand 1. Operand 2 is always updated with the original value from operand 1.
